alt: Japanese residential genkan with a lower tiled entrance and raised wooden hallway
caption: A residential genkan in Japan, viewed from the raised interior hallway. Representative residential reference; not identified as a home documented in the 1997 research source.
credit: Fg2 · Public domain · Resized for display; uncropped.
sourceDescription: Genkan    玄関  of a residence in Japan, viewed from the interior. The foreground is the raised floor of the hallway. The shoes rest on the tile floor of the  genkan . To the left of the  genkan  is the  getabako . The background of the photograph is the exterior door, shown closed.

alt: Japanese residential genkan with a lower tiled entrance and raised wooden hallway
caption: The same residential genkan viewed from outside, showing shoes on the lower tiled entry and the raised interior floor. Representative residential reference; not identified as a home documented in the 1997 research source.
credit: Fg2 · Public domain · Resized for display; uncropped.
sourceDescription: Genkan    玄関  of a house in Japan. Viewed from outdoors. At extreme left is the outside wall, then the doorjamb, and the interior wall. The  genkan  has floor tiles, and the shoes are on it. To the right of the  genkan  is the  getabako ; beyond the  genkan  is the raised interior floor of the hallway. The door with the square windows leads to the main residential area.

alt: Frankfurt Kitchen ingredient-storage bins in a museum display
caption: Ingredient storage in a Frankfurt Kitchen display at the V&A East Storehouse, London. Museum display of a historic design, not an occupied original flat.
originalFile: File:Frankfurt kitchen at V&A East Storehouse 01.jpg
sourceDescription: Kitchen designed 1926-27 by Margarete Schutte-Lihotzky and made in Germany for the Frankfurt Municipal Building Department. Considered the first fitted kitchen and the prototype of all the built-in kitchen designs that followed.. This example is installed at the V&A East Storehouse in London. Victoria and Albert Museum item number W.15-2005
